name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
description: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate (CAS 53124-00-8 ), commercially recognized as E1442 and HPDSP, is a chemically modified starch produced by combining hydroxypropylation and cross-linking treatments. It delivers superior freeze-thaw stability, viscosity control, and resistance to processing stress in food and industrial systems where native starches fall short. In food manufacturing, E1442 is the preferred thickener. It acts as a stabilizer in products such as fruit fillings, dairy desserts, soups, and sauces that undergo retort, freeze-thaw cycling, or high-shear processing. Baby food and infant formula producers rely on HPDSP. This ingredient ensures consistent texture performance across sterilization temperatures. In the paper and pulp industry, it functions as a surface sizing and coating binder, improving paper strength and printability. Textile operations apply it as a warp sizing agent to protect yarn during weaving, reducing breakage and improving throughput. Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Food-grade material is available to E1442 specifications under EU food additive regulations, with FCC -grade also commonly offered for markets requiring that standard. Industrial grades are available for paper and textile applications where food compliance is not required.
